thread.title: Austin man receives nearly three decades in prison for repeat federal drug offenses
thread.title_full: Austin man receives nearly three decades in prison for repeat federal drug offenses

author: evergreen reporter
title: Austin man receives nearly three decades in prison for repeat federal drug offenses
text:
An Austin resident, Trinity Duke Smith, 50, has been sentenced to a total of 29 years in federal prison following his third conviction for a federal drug offense. U.S. District Judge David Ezra delivered the sentence on Wednesday, imposing 324 months for possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and an additional 24 months for violating the terms of a previously imposed supervised release.
Smith had been released from prison in December 2020 and was still under supervised release when law enforcement officials searched his home on March 26, 2024. The search was conducted by the FBI and the Austin Police Department.
Authorities discovered a plastic grocery bag in Smith’s kitchen cabinet containing approximately 197 grams of suspected methamphetamine, along with items such as a digital scale, sandwich bags, latex gloves, and pieces of white insulation. In the attic, two large garbage bags were found underneath insulation containing an additional 9.2 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine.
Subsequent laboratory testing by the Drug Enforcement Administration in May 2024 confirmed that the substance from the kitchen was 188.3 grams of methamphetamine with a purity level of 91%. The substance from the attic tested as 8.899 kilograms of pure methamphetamine.
Smith was indicted on June 18, 2024, for one count of possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and pleaded guilty in August 2025.
U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas announced the sentencing. The case was investigated by the FBI, Austin Police Department, and Texas Rangers. Assistant U.S. Attorney Daniel Castillo prosecuted.
